hints.title: Per-Number Bit Iteration Obstacle
hints.text: Counting set bits for each integer from 0 to n independently by inspecting every bit position takes O(n log n) time. How can the bit count of any number relate directly to the bit count of a smaller number with one fewer bit?

hints.title: Right-Shift Subproblem Invariant
hints.text: Right-shifting a number by one removes its least significant bit, meaning countBits(i) = countBits(i >> 1) + (i & 1).

hints.title: Linear DP Bit Shift Procedure
hints.text: Allocate an array ans of size n + 1 initialized to zeros. Loop index i from 1 to n. For each i, compute ans[i] as ans[i >> 1] plus (i & 1). Return the populated array ans.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Computes set bits for all numbers in a single linear pass using bit shifts.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Calling bit_count / hamming weight on each number takes O(N * 32) bit operations rather than reusing subproblem results in O(1) operations per number.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Reusing ans[i >> 1] provides O(N) linear time with O(1) auxiliary space beyond the output array.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Explaining recurrence relation ans[i] = ans[i >> 1] + (i & 1), bitwise right shift efficiency.
